title: Explain KV caching in three sentences.

messages.content: Explain KV caching in three sentences.

Key-value caching (KV caching) is a data storage technique where frequently accessed data is stored in a smaller, faster, and more efficient data structure (e.g., a database) instead of the original source (e.g., a file). This approach reduces the load on the original source, making it more scalable and performant. By caching frequently accessed data, KV caching can improve application performance, reduce latency, and provide faster data retrieval times.
